step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified core components from the visual diagram and audio transcript:
   - External meeting applications (Meeting application A, B, C) represented as a ThirdParty entry point.
   - Amazon API Gateway as the entry point for requests.
   - AWS Lambda Post Transcript processing inbound meeting requests.
   - Amazon DynamoDB storing meeting and customer metadata.
   - Amazon S3 storing raw transcripts.
   - AWS Step Functions Workflow orchestrating the processing pipeline.
   - Map Parallelization (AWS Lambda) splitting transcripts by agendas and invoking Bedrock in parallel.
   - Amazon Bedrock (ThirdParty, as it's not present in AWS valid list) executing generative AI model summarization.
   - AWS Lambda (Aggregator) aggregating agenda-level summaries into a final summary document.
   - Amazon S3 storing final aggregated summaries.
   - AWS Lambda Get Status & Summary providing status updates and final summary responses back via API Gateway.

2. Grouped interactions into logical flows:
   - Flow 0: Meeting transcript submission and storage (Meeting App -> API Gateway -> Post Transcript Lambda -> S3 Transcripts & DynamoDB).
   - Flow 1: Processing and summarization workflow (S3 -> Step Functions -> Map Parallelization -> Bedrock & Aggregator Lambda -> S3 Summaries).
   - Flow 2: Status check and summary retrieval (API Gateway <-> Get Status & Summary Lambda <-> DynamoDB).

3. Mapped all names and service types to exact vocabulary requirements.

graph.name: Granicus GovMeetings Automated Meeting Summarization Architecture
graph.notes: Granicus GovMeetings platform uses AWS Step Functions, Lambda, Bedrock, S3, and DynamoDB to automatically divide 500+ page transcriptions into agenda items, summarize them in parallel using generative AI models, and aggregate the summary for civic clerks.

nodes.name: Meeting application A
nodes.notes: Application agnostic meeting platform input source.

nodes.name: Amazon API Gateway
nodes.notes: Entry point for summarization requests and status queries.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda Post Transcript
nodes.notes: Processes request, saves metadata to DynamoDB and uploads transcripts to S3.

nodes.name: Amazon DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Stores meeting metadata and customer configuration for 600+ customers; updated with status upon completion.

nodes.name: AWS Step Functions Workflow
nodes.notes: Orchestrates parallel map state workflow upon S3 transcript upload.

nodes.name: Map Parallelization
nodes.notes: Splits transcripts into agenda items and runs parallel summarization requests to Bedrock.

nodes.name: Amazon Bedrock
nodes.notes: Uses foundational models (e.g. Claude V3) to generate agenda-level summaries.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda (Aggregator)
nodes.notes: Aggregates individual agenda summaries into a final document.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 (Summaries)
nodes.notes: Stores completed, aggregated meeting summary documents.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda Get Status & Summary
nodes.notes: Retrieves process status and final summary for clients; preserves status in DynamoDB.

edges.notes: Meeting application sends summarization request and transcript.
API Gateway triggers Post Transcript Lambda.
Post Transcript Lambda writes meeting and customer metadata to DynamoDB.
Post Transcript Lambda uploads transcript files to S3 bucket.
S3 transcript upload triggers Step Functions workflow.
Step Functions executes Map Parallelization Lambda state.
Map Parallelization Lambda invokes Amazon Bedrock models in parallel per agenda item.
Parallel map outputs are passed to Aggregator Lambda.
Aggregator Lambda stores final aggregated summary document in S3.
API Gateway routes client status and summary requests to Get Status & Summary Lambda.
Get Status & Summary Lambda returns processing result/summary back through API Gateway.
Get Status & Summary Lambda checks and preserves status in DynamoDB.
